name: Proving you're human became the local-news product
what: Ten picks across five AI in Local News editions were about verifying humans and images: Backstory, Originator Profile, Made by Humans, Apple Reference Image, the Press Gazette unverifiable-writers investigation, and the collapse of 200+ AI 'local news' sites.
pitch: WPR's advantage over synthetic competitors is being checkably human. Prism's fake-local network collapsed on its own; what remains contestable is whether readers can verify a byline, a photo, or a submitted tip.
access: Pattern · 10 picks across 5 AI in Local News editions (08-23 to 09-14)

name: Agents look reliable because someone patches them weekly
what: Five AI Field Notes picks (09-26) plus claude plugin eval (09-11) and plugin validate (09-24) converge: the agent that 'ran flawlessly' was patched weekly, coding agents fix the failing test rather than the bug, and static CLAUDE.md files rot.
pitch: Every WPR build that runs unattended — trackers, Fire Watch, the newsletter pipeline — has this failure shape. The remedy in the picks is a harness with eval cases and validation, not longer instructions.
access: Pattern · 7 picks across 3 editions (5 concentrated in Field Notes 09-26)

name: The vendors finally shipped the guardrail layer
what: Claude Code added --restricted mode and /claude-api cost-optimize (08-28) then output and effort caps (2.1.261–269); Managed Agents added domain-restricted web tools, sandbox memory and 'auto' permissions; Messages API added on-demand compaction (09-18).
pitch: These are exactly the controls a solo operator running unattended jobs needs: bounded spend, bounded blast radius. Turning them on is an afternoon and removes a whole class of runaway-cost and wrong-site risk.
access: Pattern · 7 picks across 4 WPR AI Digest editions (08-23, 08-28, 09-12, 09-18)

name: Speech and live audio moved into the base API tier
what: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and Transcribe Live went GA (08-28), followed by Gemini 3.8 Live and Live Extended Thinking (09-18), GPT-Live-1 in the API (09-12), agentic video understanding (09-04) and OpenAI Ultrafast mode (08-23).
pitch: Fire Watch and Gavel are audio products. Transcription stopped being a separate vendor line item and became a cheap, streaming API tier — which changes both cost per hour and what 'same day' can mean.
access: Pattern · 6 picks across 5 WPR AI Digest editions (08-23 to 09-18)

name: Attribution and payment rails are being built around publishers
what: Apple reportedly paying publishers for news in Siri answers (08-23), Google's Preferred Sources button (08-24) and 'AI contribution' pilot in Search Console (09-14), the Press Gazette deals-and-lawsuits tracker (08-31), and OpenAI's journalism ecosystem expansion (09-18).
pitch: Most of this is aimed at large publishers, but Preferred Sources and the Search Console pilot are self-serve and free to check. Missing them costs nothing visible, which is why they get missed.
access: Pattern · 5 picks across 4 AI in Local News editions (08-23 to 09-18)

name: Bake off Gemini 3.5 Transcribe against the Fire Watch pipeline
what: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe (GA) and Transcribe Live, plus GPT-Live-1, make a purpose-built speech endpoint cheap enough to test against Fire Watch's dispatch audio and Gavel's meeting recordings.
pitch: Dispatch audio is short, noisy and dense with street and agency names — the case where a dedicated transcription model either clearly wins or clearly doesn't. One week settles it with real numbers.
access: Try next quarter · Fire Watch and Gavel; from 4 speech picks (08-28, 09-12, 09-18)

name: Build a 30-case failure set for Ledgers and the court tracker
what: 'Error discovery before metrics' (Field Notes 09-26) argues you collect real failures before scoring anything; claude plugin eval (2.1.269) and plugin validate (2.1.281) supply the runner and the MCP checks.
pitch: Ledgers and the court, permit and property trackers extract structured facts from messy documents, and failures currently surface when a reader notices. A fixture file turns that into a pre-deploy check.
access: Try next quarter · Ledgers and court/permit/property trackers; from 3 picks (Field Notes 09-26, Skills Radar 09-11, 09-24)

name: Publish WPR's AI policy and byline rules
what: The Austin Chronicle published a plain newsroom AI policy (09-11), SPJ proposed Code of Ethics edits for the AI age (08-23), and Made by Humans (09-14) checks copy before publication.
pitch: WPR already uses AI across most builds without a public statement of how. A one-page policy takes a week, protects the obituary platform and Ledgers from doubt, and helps with LION groups and grant applications.
access: Try next quarter · obituary platform, Gavel, newsletter; from 3 picks (08-23, 09-11, 09-14)

name: Model-name churn and office-suite AI didn't earn their space
what: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.7 Flash then 3.8 Flash arrived inside five weeks, alongside GPT-6 Astra, Ultrafast GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1 and Sakana Fugu Max — plus 30 Tools Radar picks like custom web fonts in Sheets charts.
pitch: None of these changed a WPR build. The releases that mattered were narrow: Transcribe, cost-optimize, plugin eval, Scrapling. Frontier naming and Workspace feature drip can be skimmed or skipped.
access: Fading · ~12 model-release picks plus 30 Workspace/ChatGPT picks, none traceable to a build change
